'''Gordon D Love''' (born 1967) is a British physicist. Love is a professor of computer science and physics at the University of Leeds and is the head of the University of Leeds' School of Computer Science.<ref>{{Cite web |last=Sciences |first=Faculty of Engineering and Physical |title=Professor Gordon Love {{!}} School of Computing {{!}} University of Leeds |url=https://eps.leeds.ac.uk/computing/staff/13563/professor-gordon-love |access-date=2024-01-18 |website=eps.leeds.ac.uk |language=en}}</ref> Love is a former professor at the [[Durham University Department of Physics]] and a specialist in [[optics]] research. He is noted in particular for his work in [[adaptive optics]].<ref>{{cite web |title=The Material World 24/10/2002 |url=http://www.bbc.co.uk/radio4/science/thematerialworld_20021024.shtml |website=[[BBC Radio 4]] |access-date=30 January 2021}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |title=Atmospheric and Ocean Optics |url=https://www.osapublishing.org/ao/journal/ao/anniversary/editorspicks/atmospheric-ocean-optics.cfm |website=OSA |access-date=30 January 2021}}</ref>

He is a council member of the [[Institute of Physics]] and past board member of the [[European Optical Society]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Council |url=http://www.iop.org/about/governance/council/page_38744.html |website=[[Institute of Physics]] |access-date=30 January 2021 |language=en}}</ref>

==Education==
Love earned both his [[Bachelor of Science]] and doctorate from [[Durham University]].<ref>{{cite journal |title=Academic Staff: Physics |journal=Durham University Calendar 1999-2000 |date=2000 |volume=1 |page=187 |url=http://reed.dur.ac.uk/xtf/view?docId=bookreader/DU_Calendars/1999/v1/v1.xml#page/187/mode/2up |access-date=30 January 2021}}</ref> He was an undergraduate at [[Van Mildert College, Durham|Van Mildert College]].<ref>{{cite web |title=Professor GD Love |url=https://www.dur.ac.uk/physics/staff/profiles/?id=246 |website=Durham University |access-date=30 January 2021}}</ref> He attended Ralph Thoresby High School in Leeds.
